record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
record.original_question: For a G2-holonomy manifold, after constructing a BRST-type cohomology of the smooth chiral de Rham complex with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces, what is the character of that cohomology, does it provide an analog of the elliptic genus for G2 manifolds, and does the resulting series converge and have modular properties?

evidence.quote: The second problem is to study its character, this would be the analog of the elliptic genus for a G2 manifold.

It follows that if the answer to the question 4.21 is affirmative, we can attach the formal series χM (τ) = q−21/48strH(ΩchM ,Q−0 ) qL+0 , q = e2πiτ, and ask if this series converges and has modular properties.
Note that since we have two commuting Virasoros: T+, X+ we may promote the above function to a two variable trace by computing the joint eigenspaces of T+0 and X+0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact 7-dimensional Riemannian manifold with holonomy group contained in the exceptional Lie group $G_2$. Associated to $M$ is the smooth chiral de Rham complex $\Omega^{ch}_M$, a sheaf of topological vertex superalgebras whose space of global sections $H = H^0(M, \Omega^{ch}_M)$ carries an action of the Shatashvili–Vafa $G_2$ superconformal algebra. In particular, $H$ contains two commuting Virasoro fields $T^{+}(z)$ and $X^{+}(z)$ (with zero modes $T^{+}_0$, $X^{+}_0$) and a distinguished odd field whose zero mode $Q^{+}_0$ squares to zero, providing a BRST-type differential on $H$.

Assume that the cohomology $\mathcal{H}(M) := H^*(H, Q^{+}_0)$ has finite-dimensional conformal weight spaces with respect to the residual Virasoro action (so each joint eigenspace of $T^{+}_0$ and $X^{+}_0$ on the cohomology is finite-dimensional).

Define the formal series
$$\chi_M(\tau) = q^{-21/48}\,\mathrm{str}_{\mathcal{H}(M)}\, q^{L^{+}_0}, \qquad q = e^{2\pi i \tau},$$
where $L^{+}_0$ is the zero mode of the residual Virasoro and $\mathrm{str}$ is the supertrace, as well as the two-variable refinement
$$\chi_M(\tau, z) = q^{-21/48}\,\mathrm{str}_{\mathcal{H}(M)}\, q^{T^{+}_0}\, y^{X^{+}_0}, \qquad y = e^{2\pi i z},$$
obtained from the joint $(T^{+}_0, X^{+}_0)$ grading.

Determine:
(i) an explicit formula for $\chi_M(\tau)$ (and for $\chi_M(\tau,z)$) in terms of topological/geometric invariants of $M$, thereby producing a $G_2$-analog of the elliptic genus;
(ii) whether the series $\chi_M(\tau)$ converges in the upper half plane $\{\mathrm{Im}\,\tau > 0\}$;
(iii) whether $\chi_M(\tau)$ (respectively $\chi_M(\tau,z)$) is a modular (respectively Jacobi) form with respect to a suitable congruence subgroup, and identify that group together with the weight and index.
artifact.category_tag: Chiral de Rham complex and G2 elliptic genus
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for results on a $G_2$ analog of the elliptic genus arising from BRST cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex returned results on the Calabi–Yau (N=2) case (Borisov–Libgober, Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob and follow-ups) and the orbifold/toric case, but no source establishing convergence, an explicit formula, or modular properties of the proposed $G_2$ character. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Elliptic Genera of singular varieties, orbifold elliptic genus and chiral de Rham complex
status_evidence.snippet: BRST cohomology yields the cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex and the elliptic genus is computed as a supertrace.
status_evidence.claim: The Calabi–Yau analog (N=2 elliptic genus from chiral de Rham) is established, but no $G_2$ analog is provided.

status_evidence.title: Equivariant cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex in equivariant/Calabi–Yau settings.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature treats Calabi–Yau-type settings; no construction of a modular $G_2$ character is given.

status_evidence.title: The Global Sections of Chiral de Rham Complexes on Closed Complex Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025/2026) work computes global sections in the curve case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity continues but does not address the $G_2$ character/modularity question.
